title: SWEN3204 Assignment 2 – Marking Rubric

levels.label: Excellent
levels.desc: Two attributes that clearly matter most are chosen and justified from the scenario. Both scenarios have all six parts and both response measures are measurable.

levels.label: Proficient
levels.desc: Suitable attributes are chosen with some justification. Scenarios are mostly complete but one is missing a part or has a response measure that is not measurable.

levels.label: Developing
levels.desc: Attributes are named with little or no justification, or the scenarios are not in six-part form or are not measurable.

levels.label: Missing
levels.desc: Not attempted or irrelevant.

levels.label: Excellent
levels.desc: A clear recommendation justified by at least two trade-offs that are specific to the scenario (team size, load profile, known problems). The downside of the recommendation is acknowledged.

levels.label: Proficient
levels.desc: A clear recommendation with two trade-offs, but one is generic or not linked to the scenario, or no downside is acknowledged.

levels.label: Developing
levels.desc: A recommendation with only one trade-off, or with generic textbook advantages and disadvantages only.

levels.label: Missing
levels.desc: Not attempted or no recommendation.

levels.label: Excellent
levels.desc: Parts (a), (b) and (c) are all correct with working shown, to the requested precision.

levels.label: Proficient
levels.desc: The method is correct throughout but there is one arithmetic or rounding slip, or exactly one part is incorrect.

levels.label: Developing
levels.desc: The series calculation is attempted but two or more parts are incorrect, or working is not shown.

levels.label: Missing
levels.desc: Not attempted or no correct element.

levels.label: Excellent
levels.desc: An appropriate pattern is named, its mechanism is explained correctly, it is applied to the outage, and at least one drawback or tuning consideration is given.

levels.label: Proficient
levels.desc: An appropriate pattern is named and explained correctly, but it is only loosely applied to the outage or no drawback or tuning consideration is given.

levels.label: Developing
levels.desc: A pattern is named but the explanation is incorrect or very thin.

levels.label: Missing
levels.desc: Not attempted or an unsuitable pattern.

levels.label: Excellent
levels.desc: Both choices are justified, the CAP theorem is used correctly, and a suitable concrete technique is named for each case.

levels.label: Proficient
levels.desc: Both choices are reasonable and techniques are named, but the CAP theorem is explained incorrectly or imprecisely, or one technique is missing.

levels.label: Developing
levels.desc: Choices are stated with little justification, or the CAP theorem is not used.

levels.label: Missing
levels.desc: Not attempted.

levels.label: Excellent
levels.desc: Context, Decision and Consequences are all present and specific to the scenario, with at least one positive and one negative consequence.

levels.label: Proficient
levels.desc: All three sections are present but the consequences are one-sided (no negative consequence) or the context is generic.

levels.label: Developing
levels.desc: One or more sections are missing or the record does not describe a decision.

levels.label: Missing
levels.desc: Not attempted.

levels.label: Excellent
levels.desc: Every answer is within 150 words, terminology is precise, the required headings are used and sources are cited in IEEE style.

levels.label: Proficient
levels.desc: Clear writing, but one answer exceeds the word limit or there are minor citation or formatting problems.

levels.label: Developing
levels.desc: Several answers exceed the word limit, or the writing is hard to follow, or sources are not cited.

levels.label: Missing
levels.desc: Format requirements ignored.

notes: Award whole marks only. Each criterion is marked within the mark range of the level that best describes the answer.
